The Moroccan regime was very unsettled by the Rif protests.
When the ship arrives in port it makes the people unsettled.
The horses are unsettled about the gunshots.
Thinking about her future, she is unsettled.
We shouldn't leave the matter unsettled.
Ziri lived in an unsettled territory.
They left the situation unsettled.

d: A conscious choice or decision.
The mental power or ability of choosing; the will.
A concept that distinguishes whether or not the subject or agent intended something.
e: Out of all the factors that can influence a person’s decision, none can match the power of his or her own volition.

fr.t: Kevin McCarthy doesn't do anything of his own volition.
Rima accepted Adriano’s proposal by her own volition.
We did not come into this world of our own volition.
Mary had gone to the police of her own volition.
He confessed to the crime of his own volition.
He left of his own volition.
I very much hope that I did not pressure him, but that he came with us of his own volition.
Despite my parents' preference, I have decided to attend an out-of-state college on my own volition.

d: A low intermittent sob.
To cry or sob softly and intermittently.
To cry with a low, whining, broken voice; to whine; to complain.
To say something in a whimpering manner.
e: The lonely puppy began to whimper as soon as we left the room.
“Master, please don’t punish me!” he whimpered.

fr.t: This is the way the world ends. Not with a bang but a whimper.
Ziri heard a whimper in the distance. It sounded like a dog crying.
Whimper all you want. Nobody will do this for you, anyway. Don't even get your hopes up.
Nine-month-old David drops to his knees, crawls toward a bottle of milk on the counter and begins to whimper.
